title: Derived restriction of scalars commutes with $Rf_*$
statement:
Let $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings such that for every
scheme $X$ the extension of scalars $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}$ preserves finite limits
($\Lambda'_X$ flat over $\Lambda_X$; [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]), and let
$f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. With $Rf_*$ the derived pushforward of module objects
([sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]) there is a natural isomorphism

$$
D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y})\circ Rf_*\;\cong\;Rf_*\circ D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_X})\colon
D(\Mod_{\Lambda'_X})\longrightarrow D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}).
$$

proof.text: Write $U_W=\operatorname{Res}_{a_W}$ for $W=X,Y$, $F'=f_*^{\Lambda'}$ and $F=f_*^{\Lambda}$. These are functors between the abelian categories of module objects in abelian sheaves, with the closed symmetric monoidal tensor structure of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Tensoring preserves finite coproducts by the cited closedness statement, hence finite biproducts; the formula $g+h=\nabla\circ(g\oplus h)\circ\Delta$ shows that tensoring is additive. By clause 4 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], $U_X$ and $U_Y$ are exact; this does not require flatness. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to each $U_W$. Thus $U_W$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and $D(U_W)(QK)\cong Q(U_WK)$ naturally in the complex $K$; denote this isomorphism by $\rho^W_K$, where $Q$ denotes localization in the relevant module category. In particular, exact restriction is applied to complexes termwise, without choosing a further resolution.

source.place: First sentence: exact restriction and levelwise derivation; supporting Stacks Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), (3)-(4)

proof.text:
For a complex $K$ of $\Lambda'_X$-module objects choose a K-injective resolution $s:K\to I$, as used in the definition [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] of $RF'$. The hypothesis that $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_W}$ preserves finite limits for every scheme $W$ is exactly the hypothesis of [lem-sfb-comap-preserves-k-injectives], so $U_XI$ is K-injective in $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$. Step 1 shows that $U_Xs$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Hence $I$ and $U_XI$ compute the respective pushforwards: [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] gives $RF'(QK)\cong Q(F'I)$ and $RF(D(U_X)(QK))\cong Q(FU_XI)$. Write $\eta'$ and $\eta$ for the natural units of these two right derived functors. Specify the canonical isomorphisms just used as
$$\alpha_s=(\eta'_I)^{-1}\circ RF'(Qs):RF'(QK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(F'I),$$
$$\beta_s=(\eta_{U_XI})^{-1}\circ RF(Q(U_Xs))\circ RF(\rho^X_K):RF D(U_X)(QK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(FU_XI).$$
All factors are invertible: the units are invertible on K-injectives, and $s,U_Xs$ are quasi-isomorphisms. No K-injectivity of $F'I$ is required.

source.place: Last two sentences: exact restriction preserves K-injectives and the same resolution computes the composite; supporting Stacks Tags 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined) and 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies)

proof.text:
Let $\theta:U_YF'\xrightarrow{\sim}FU_X$ be the underived natural isomorphism of [def-sfb-comap-lower-star-iso]. Apply its component in each degree of $I$. Its naturality for $d_I^n:I^n\to I^{n+1}$ says that these components commute with the differentials, giving an isomorphism of complexes $\theta_I:U_YF'I\xrightarrow{\sim}FU_XI$. Define the desired component $c_{QK}$ to be the composite
$$D(U_Y)RF'(QK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(U_YF'I)\xrightarrow{Q(\theta_I)}Q(FU_XI)\xrightarrow{\sim}RF D(U_X)(QK).$$
The first arrow is $\rho^Y_{F'I}\circ D(U_Y)(\alpha_s)$ and the last is $\beta_s^{-1}$, with the maps of steps 1 and 2. Every arrow is an isomorphism, so this defines an invertible component of the claimed type in $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$.

source.place: Middle sentence: derive the underived natural isomorphism; degreewise construction, with the resolution identifications in the surrounding sentences

proof.text:
We verify naturality and independence of the chosen resolution. For complexes $K,L$ choose resolutions $s:K\to I$ and $t:L\to J$ as above. For any derived morphism $u:QK\to QL$, the bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives a unique homotopy class $h:I\to J$ such that $Qh=Qt\circ u\circ(Qs)^{-1}$. The natural units in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] satisfy $RF'(Qh)\circ\eta'_I=\eta'_J\circ Q(F'h)$ and $RF(Q(U_Xh))\circ\eta_{U_XI}=\eta_{U_XJ}\circ Q(FU_Xh)$. Substituting $Qh=Qt\circ u\circ(Qs)^{-1}$ and the definitions of $\alpha,\beta$ in step 2 gives
$$\alpha_t\circ RF'(u)=Q(F'h)\circ\alpha_s,\qquad \beta_t\circ RF D(U_X)(u)=Q(FU_Xh)\circ\beta_s.$$
For the second equation use the naturality of $\rho^X$ from step 1 to identify $D(U_X)(Qh)$ with $Q(U_Xh)$, and $U_XJ$ is K-injective by step 2. Here $h$ denotes any chain-map representative of its homotopy class. The naturality of $\theta$ gives the equality of chain maps
$$FU_X(h)\circ\theta_I=\theta_J\circ U_YF'(h),$$
Applying $Q$ to this equality, using the two displayed identities and the naturality of $\rho^Y$ on $F'h$, gives $RF D(U_X)(u)\circ c_{QK}=c_{QL}\circ D(U_Y)RF'(u)$. This equality depends only on the homotopy class: an additive functor sends a homotopy $h-h'=dv+vd$ to $Fh-Fh'=F(d)F(v)+F(v)F(d)$, which is again a homotopy. For a second resolution $s':K\to I'$, apply the same bijection to $Qs'\circ(Qs)^{-1}$; it is represented by a homotopy equivalence $I\to I'$ (the inverse is represented by the inverse derived morphism, and faithfulness gives the two identities up to homotopy). The displayed naturality equality for this comparison identifies the two formulas for $c_{QK}$. Thus the components descend independently of resolutions to all objects and morphisms of the unbounded derived category, and form the required natural isomorphism. This uses the underived naturality of [def-sfb-comap-lower-star-iso], not just equality of underlying objects.

split_report.blueprint: Realizes the full proof in def-sfb-derived-comap-lower-star-iso.proof.md: step 1 is the exact levelwise restriction in the first sentence; step 2 is the K-injective computation in the final two sentences; step 3 constructs the middle underived comparison degreewise; step 4 verifies naturality and resolution independence of these composites. reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NJ-3050a2768 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: one item, no new nodes, and no fixes or tool_uses needed. The statement matches the main-20261015 blueprint .md word for word, with the same flatness hypothesis on Ext_{a_X}, layer-B module objects, the unbounded D(Mod_{Lambda'_X})->D(Mod_{Lambda_Y}), and the same orientation; it is not weakened. The four steps follow the .proof.md route: exact levelwise Res, then the underived comap-lower-star iso, then K-injective preservation. Step 1: sheaf-tensor closedness gives an additive tensor, so change-of-scalars clause 4 gives exact Res, and the exact-factorization Mathlib leaf gives rho (Stacks 015F, derived.tex:5884). Step 2: the hypothesis matches lem-sfb-comap-preserves-k-injectives word for word, the unit eta of def-sfb-right-derived-functor is invertible on K-injectives, and the directions in alpha_s and beta_s are correct (Stacks 070Y, 070K). Step 3: theta has the right orientation, and naturality on the differentials gives a chain isomorphism. Step 4: I recomputed both naturality identities from the eta, rho and theta naturalities and the K-injective Hom bijection, which is a Mathlib leaf (Stacks 070I (1)=>(3), derived.tex:9632); resolution independence follows with u=id. Route: the only statements used are from the item's own unit or are Mathlib leaves, and the rest are definitions; there is no cycle and no SGA. Duplicates: the upper-star comparison and the underived node are different statements. Small cases checked: a=id, f=id, the zero complex, degree-0 complexes, empty X, and Z->Z/2, which falls outside the hypothesis. Minor and accepted: existence of K-injective resolutions in Mod_{Lambda'_X} is presupposed by the cited Rf_* definition rather than cited separately.
